questions.title: Finite entropic transport: optimization, sampling limits and reproducible inference
questions.description: Develop a complete source-assisted statistical study of entropy-regularized transport between two unknown distributions on fixed finite supports. For strictly positive population probability vectors a and b, a fixed finite nonnegative cost matrix C, and fixed epsilon>0, the estimand is V_epsilon(a,b)=min over nonnegative couplings P with row sums a and column sums b of sum(C_ij P_ij)+epsilon sum(P_ij(log P_ij-1)), with 0 log 0=0. This exact objective, not the transport-only cost and not a debiased Sinkhorn divergence, is the inferential target. Develop reviewable Markdown/LaTeX definitions, existence/uniqueness and interiority reasoning, primal-dual optimality, a justified numerical method, and a differentiability argument on the two simplex tangent spaces. From two independent multinomial samples with possibly unequal sample sizes, derive consistency, a nondegenerate normal limit, a consistent variance estimate and an asymptotic 95% Wald interval for V_epsilon. State the conditions needed for these claims, distinguish optimization error from sampling error, and do not transfer the fixed-epsilon result to epsilon tending to zero or to a degenerate first-order variance. Implement a new Python estimator est_entropic_transport according to the interface below using numerical primitives, not POT or a prebuilt OT solver. Useful scratch computation, finite-difference checks or counterexample searches are model choices and may revise theory or code before independent review. After stable current theory and code are independently accepted, freeze confirmatory multinomial designs with at least two different interior distribution pairs, unequal sample sizes and nonzero asymptotic variance. Use at least 1000 independent sample pairs per design and a pre-result precision target of Monte Carlo standard error at most 0.01 for coverage. Compare empirical 95% interval coverage, estimation bias and uncertainty calibration against the exact population regularized value, and inspect marginal/optimality accuracy. Freeze seeds, sample sizes, epsilon, numerical tolerances and acceptance criteria before confirmation; an unmet criterion remains a gap rather than permitting outcome-driven extension. Separately execute the supplied pinned POT 0.9.6.post1 fixed-support example through the source tool, read ot_example_result.json and both raw streams, and report original exact/regularized transport costs, coupling marginal errors, environment and numerical warnings. The launcher executes unchanged author code with Agg and exports numerical plans; no figure is exported or visually assessed. Do not claim original hardware timings, a historical environment, or reproduction of every experiment in the statistical papers. The package baseline does not replace new solver implementation or fresh statistical confirmation. Attribute permitted source assistance; this is known-result development, not blind rediscovery or novelty. Lean is not required. Complete theory, code, confirmation, source reproduction and an honest final report are all required, without prescribing a fixed research order or number of derivation steps.

source.primary_authority: Bigot, Cazelles and Papadakis (2019), Central limit theorems for entropy-regularized optimal transport on finite spaces and statistical applications; Cuturi (2013); POT 0.9.6.post1 public code. Translate objective conventions explicitly.

request_fields.name: source_counts
request_fields.edge_cases: Qualification and confirmation use strictly positive observed counts; no malformed-input tournament is imposed.
request_fields.meaning: First independent multinomial sample. Its total is its sample size, not a probability normalization constant to discard.

request_fields.name: target_counts
request_fields.edge_cases: The two total counts need not agree; do not pool or pair the independent samples.

request_fields.name: cost
request_fields.indexing: Rows correspond to source_counts and columns to target_counts.
request_fields.edge_cases: Rectangular supports are valid. Cost need not be symmetric.
request_fields.meaning: Fixed ground cost, not estimated or renormalized by the procedure.

request_fields.name: epsilon
request_fields.edge_cases: Fixed positive regularization, not a sample-size-dependent sequence.
request_fields.meaning: Coefficient of sum P(log P-1) in the exact frozen objective.

response_fields.name: coupling
response_fields.edge_cases: Report numerical failure honestly if the solver does not converge.
response_fields.meaning: Computed entropically regularized optimal coupling of the empirical marginals.
response_fields.normalization: Row and column sums match the two separately normalized count vectors.

response_fields.name: regularized_value
response_fields.edge_cases: May be negative; do not clip or substitute another distance.
response_fields.meaning: Full objective evaluated on the returned coupling, including epsilon sum P(log P-1).
response_fields.normalization: Probability-mass scale with the exact -1 entropy convention.

response_fields.name: transport_cost
response_fields.meaning: sum C_ij P_ij for the returned coupling.

response_fields.name: source_potential
response_fields.edge_cases: Any consistent additive gauge is allowed.
response_fields.meaning: Dual row multiplier using L=objective+f dot(a-P1)+g dot(b-P^T1).
response_fields.normalization: No implicit division by either sample size.

response_fields.name: target_potential
response_fields.edge_cases: Gauge must be coupled consistently to source_potential.
response_fields.meaning: Dual column multiplier under the same Lagrangian convention.
response_fields.normalization: No implicit division by either sample size.

response_fields.name: standard_error
response_fields.edge_cases: Zero first-order variance does not justify a nondegenerate normal assertion.
response_fields.meaning: Consistent plug-in standard error for the full regularized value under the two independent multinomial samples.
response_fields.normalization: Use each actual sample size; report standard error, not variance or a sqrt(n)-scaled variance.

response_fields.name: ci_lower
response_fields.meaning: Lower endpoint of the derived asymptotic two-sided 95% Wald interval.
response_fields.normalization: Same scale and target as regularized_value.

response_fields.name: ci_upper
response_fields.meaning: Upper endpoint of the derived asymptotic two-sided 95% Wald interval.
response_fields.normalization: Same scale and target as regularized_value.

invariants.meaning: Do not mutate the request or call POT/prebuilt OT solvers, hidden references, network, or filesystem data. Numerical primitives from NumPy/SciPy are allowed. Additional honest diagnostics are allowed.
Coupling, potentials, full value, transport-only diagnostic and interval describe the same empirical problem. Gauge changes may not change the value or standard error.

The procedure owns its numerical method, convergence checks and useful diagnostics. Do not substitute population marginals, reference values or nominal coverage. Separate numerical tolerance from statistical error.

empirical_claims.meaning: Freeze at least two distinct interior multinomial distribution pairs with unequal sample sizes, fixed epsilon, nonzero first-order variance, at least 1000 independent repetitions per design, seeds, solver tolerances and criteria. Target coverage MCSE <=0.01; no post-outcome extension.

Assess actual 95% interval coverage for the population full regularized value, bias, standard-error calibration and coupling feasibility across independent repetitions. Do not compare intervals to transport-only cost or count solver iterations as replications.
Report unmet criteria and numerical errors; finite simulation and original-package execution are not proofs, exact finite-sample coverage, arbitrary epsilon->0 results or novelty.

estimator_execution_contract.termination_guarantee: Use a finite explicit numerical convergence limit and report unresolved failure instead of fabricating an optimum. Research order and exploratory tool use are model-selected.
